For any step $\theta^+=\theta-hg$, $0<h\le\eta$, whose segment stays in the ball, put $\psi(s)=L(\theta-sg)$ for $0\le s\le h$. Then $\psi'(0)=-\|g\|^2$ and $|\psi''(s)|\le S\|g\|^2$. By [F2], $L^+=L-h\|g\|^2+\int_0^h(h-s)\psi''(s)\,ds\le L-h(1-Sh/2)\|g\|^2\le(1-h\lambda/2)L$. If $L>0$, nonnegativity of $L^+$ gives $h\lambda/2\le1$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
operations.new: 1.1 Write $g=\nabla L=J^Tr$. Since $JJ^T\succeq J_*J_*^T$, $\|g\|^2=r^TJJ^Tr\ge(\lambda/2)\|r\|^2=\lambda L$ in the ball. For any step $\theta^+=\theta-hg$, $0<h\le\eta$, whose segment stays in the ball, put $\psi(s)=L(\theta-sg)$ for $0\le s\le h$. Then $\psi'(0)=-\|g\|^2$ and $\psi''(s)=g^TH_sg$, where $H_s=\nabla^2L(\theta-sg)$. By Euclidean Cauchy–Schwarz [F4] and the induced norm [F3], $|g^TH_sg|\le\|g\|\|H_sg\|\le\|g\|\|H_s\|\|g\|\le S\|g\|^2$; for $g=0$ the same bound is immediate. By [F2], $L^+=L-h\|g\|^2+\int_0^h(h-s)\psi''(s)\,ds\le L-h(1-Sh/2)\|g\|^2\le(1-h\lambda/2)L$. If $L>0$, nonnegativity of $L^+$ gives $h\lambda/2\le1$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

operations.old: 3.2 Now assume $H\ge2$. For $1\le h<H$, let $Q(h)$ assert both that rows $i,j$ of $S^{(h)}$ coincide and that $b_i^{(h)}=b_j^{(h)}$. The base $S^{(0)}=K^{(0)}$ has equal rows by step 1.1. At layer $1$, this equality and symmetry make the pair covariance matrices for indices $(i,\ell)$ and $(j,\ell)$ identical for every $\ell$, and give $S_{ii}^{(0)}=S_{jj}^{(0)}$. Hence the Gaussian marginal means agree, so the defining formulas give $S_{i\ell}^{(1)}=S_{j\ell}^{(1)}$ for every $\ell$ and $b_i^{(1)}=b_j^{(1)}$; this proves $Q(1)$. For $2\le h<H$, assume $Q(h-1)$. Symmetry and equal rows of $S^{(h-1)}$ give equal columns, so the covariance matrices for $(i,\ell)$ and $(j,\ell)$ coincide and $\mu_i^{(h-1)}=\mu_j^{(h-1)}$. In the mean recursion this gives $b_i^{(h)}=b_j^{(h)}$. In the second-moment recursion, the old-row terms agree, the terms $b_i^{(h-1)}\mu_\ell^{(h-1)}+b_\ell^{(h-1)}\mu_i^{(h-1)}$ agree with their $j$-row counterparts, and the Gaussian activation expectations agree; thus $S_{i\ell}^{(h)}=S_{j\ell}^{(h)}$ for every $\ell$. This proves $Q(h)$. Finite induction gives $Q(H-1)$. The terminal residual formula then has equal prefactors $S_{i\ell}^{(H-1)}=S_{j\ell}^{(H-1)}$ and equal derivative expectations because the corresponding pair covariance matrices coincide. Therefore the terminal residual rows coincide. [A1, F1, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra, discharge-induction]
